transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-29
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Sofia Reyes (Abyss, Head of ML), Marco Chen (Abyss, Staff Engineer), Olivia Park (Abyss, PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed model selection for mixed workloads; customer asked about 8k vs 32k context impacts and tool-calling. Security & private deployment questions surfaced.

Links shared: https://redwood.ai/share/security-pack.pdf, https://redwood.ai/share/poc-scoping-template.pdf, https://redwood.ai/share/benchmark-2026.xlsx

Transcript Body:
00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, then we want to understand your primary workloads, is it chat, batch, embeddings, or a mix?
00:12 Sofia: Hi, yeah thanks. We're primarily chat for our customer support assistant and then nightly batch summarization for long docs. Also multilingual, we support English, Japanese and Spanish and a small amount of Arabic.
00:27 Marco: And technical constraints: we have spikes to ~200 rps during business hours, average latency target for chat is <300ms p50, and we want to keep token costs reasonable.
00:40 Samir: Got it. Jules will cover architecture and model tradeoffs.
00:45 Jules: Hey all. A few quick clarifying Qs — when you say long docs, what's the typical context length you need? You mentioned long, like 8k? 32k? 64k?
00:57 Olivia: Mostly 8k today, but we are evaluating 32k for multi-doc summarization and long dialogue threads. We'll probably pilot 32k for a subset of users.
01:12 Jules: Ok that maps well to Redwood's model recommendations: some open models do well at 8k out of the box; for 32k we typically recommend model families that have verified extended context or to use chunking with KV cache. There's tradeoffs on latency and cost.
01:30 Marco: On the open model front, which ones do you recommend? We're cost-sensitive so fully managed GPT-like isn't ideal.
01:40 Samir: We commonly evaluate Mistral, Mistral-chat variants, and some Llama-family open checkpoints, plus Redwood-verified variants. For 32k we verify performance profiles — and we can provide a matrix.
01:55 Sofia: Are there big differences in tool-calling / function calling across these open models? We rely on tool-calling to hit internal APIs and to run RAG pipelines.
02:06 Jules: Good question. Function-calling support varies; some models support structured output natively, others need wrappers. Redwood provides function-calling layer and adapter so hosted and dedicated can surface tool-calls consistently. There is sometimes a mismatch in tokenization or names, so you might see odd parsing errors — transcription note, I said tokenize not token...
02:30 Marco: We need deterministic structured outputs for our internal order API. Can Redwood guarantee schema enforcement?
02:38 Jules: We offer structured output tooling plus a validation layer. In practice, for strict schemas we recommend a small post-parse validation step in your service, but Redwood's function-calling and schema hints reduce errors significantly.
02:55 Olivia: On private deployment: we have compliance folks asking for VPC-only access, KMS integration, and audit logs. What's the difference between hosted and dedicated here?
03:06 Samir: Hosted is easiest to get started — fast onboarding, managed KMS options and SOC 2. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with better latency isolation and can be set up with customer-managed KMS in many cases. Private (VPC/on-prem) gives you full network control and on-prem options but is a heavier lift operationally.
03:28 Sofia: Do you support customer-managed HSM? Our security team prefers HSM-backed keys.
03:33 Samir: Yes, HSM/KMS integrations are supported for Private and Dedicated in most configs; we'll send the KMS integration docs.
03:41 Marco: About latency, if we go with Dedicated and pin a lower latency SLO, how does that compare cost-wise vs Hosted?
03:49 Jules: Dedicated reduces variability and can give better p50/p95 latency but has commit costs. For sustained high QPS it's often cheaper. Hosted has elasticity and lower commit overhead but you may see higher p95 variability during spikes. We can model that — I can put numbers in the POC spreadsheet.
04:10 Sofia: For multilingual: any models with confirmed high quality for Japanese and Arabic? We saw different performance across vendors.
04:18 Jules: Some open models are trained multilingual, but quality varies. We have model evals and per-language benchmarks. We can share our internal eval summary and recommend a shortlist. For Arabic, in particular, you may need fine-tuning or instruction tuning for best results.
04:35 Marco: Regarding tokenization and cost, is there anything special with 32k context? Are tokens counted differently?
04:41 Samir: Tokens are tokens; cost scales with tokens. But some quantized variants and batching strategies reduce per-token cost. Also, prefix caching (KV cache) can amortize cost for repeated contexts.
04:57 Olivia: Can you explain prefix caching and KV cache? I sometimes see docs call it 'KV cash' in notes :)
05:04 Jules: Sure — KV cache stores key/value attention states for previously seen prefixes so subsequent generations are faster and avoid recomputing earlier layers. It helps a lot for chat where prompt context is repeated. Sometimes auto-transcriptions spell it wrong, yes.
05:20 Sofia: Are there restrictions on model variants for KV cache? I.e., do quantized models still support it?
05:28 Jules: Many quantized variants do support it, but some extreme 4-bit paths have limitations; we test kernels and will recommend compatible quantization profiles.
05:40 Marco: Security again — audit logs and retention. Our legal team wants 7 years for access logs for certain clients. Is that configurable?
05:49 Samir: Audit logs retention is configurable for Dedicated and Private. Hosted has default retention but can be extended with add-on packages. We'll share the audit log SLA in the security pack.
06:05 Olivia: About POC scope — we want to validate latency and cost for both 8k and 32k, and test function calling reliability against our internal order API. Also multilingual quality for Japanese & Arabic.
06:21 Samir: Sounds good. Proposed POC: 2 weeks — baseline hosted run + 1 week on dedicated pools (if you choose) with the same prompt sets, measure p50/p95, throughput, and structured output error rate. We'll provide tooling to run benchmarks.
06:35 Marco: For the benchmark, do you need sample data in advance?
06:39 Jules: Yes send us prompt sets and expected QPS and a sample of long documents. If you want we can run a short warm-up test on hosted to collect telemetry.
06:50 Sofia: Timeline — security review takes 2-3 weeks on our side. We're aiming for a POC in mid-May.
06:58 Samir: Ok we'll try to align. I'll send pricing and security docs tomorrow, Jules will share the POC template and benchmark sheet.
07:08 Olivia: Anything else from your side?
07:12 Marco: One more infra question — do you support VPC peering or private link into our cloud?
07:18 Samir: Yes for Dedicated and Private we offer VPC peering and private connectivity options; we'll include network diagrams in the pack.
07:26 Sofia: For governance — RBAC and SSO?
07:29 Jules: SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC are supported. We'll include docs.
07:35 (background cross talk)
07:40 Speaker 2: there's a note — competitor question, are you comparing to Vertex or Anthropic?
07:45 Olivia: We're running a parallel eval with Anthropic for safety behavior and Vertex for infra simplicity.
07:52 Samir: Makes sense. We can provide head-to-head perf numbers on our verified models.
08:00 Marco: Any gotchas with on-prem installation?
08:05 Jules: On-prem needs a bit more ops bandwidth; network egress and data localization are in your control but you'll need to provision GPU infra and potentially accept maintenance windows. For air-gapped, we have an on-prem package but it requires planning.
08:21 Sofia: For pricing, is there a minimum commitment for Dedicated?
08:25 Samir: Yes there are reserved capacity commitments for Dedicated — monthly/annual. We'll surface the tiers and burst options in the pricing deck.
08:36 Olivia: For POC, can we do a no-commit hosted baseline and then try a short dedicated pilot?
08:40 Samir: Absolutely. That's our typical path — start hosted, then if traffic justifies move to Dedicated or Private.
08:47 Jules: I'll also note potential optimization levers we'll test: batching config, quantization profiles, prefix caching and model variant selection.
09:00 Sofia: Great. Recap for us — send pricing, security pack, POC template, benchmark sheet, and we'll share prompts and QPS estimates.
09:12 Samir: Yep. I'll send those items. We'll also propose dates for the POC scoping session next week.
09:20 (end of meeting)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions (Speaker 2), filler words, and small mis-spellings of product terms (KV cash for KV cache). The transcript preserves conversational flow and some interruptions.
